heroHeadline: Day 592: Sheinbaum-Trump 'Cordial and Excellent' Phone Call; Bilateral Meeting Set for May 27; Tren Maya Cargo Groundbreaking at Puerto Progreso (26,200 Jobs); Mexico Backs Bachelet for UN SG
heroSubtitle: On May 16, 2026 (Day 592, Saturday), three significant developments defined the day. Most consequentially, President Sheinbaum and U.S. President Trump held a direct bilateral phone call that Sheinbaum publicly described as 'cordial and excellent.' The conversation covered security cooperation and USMCA trade negotiations — the two leaders agreed that U.S. envoys will visit Mexico and that a formal bilateral meeting will take place on May 27, 2026. The call came amid a diplomatic de-escalation arc: on May 11, the U.S. formally recognized Mexico's 'Attention to Causes' security strategy, and the first formal USMCA negotiating round is confirmed for the week of May 25 in Mexico City. The EU-Mexico Summit on May 22 — where Mexico will sign the modernized EU-Mexico Global Agreement — approaches as a key trade diversification milestone. Also on May 16: Sheinbaum was on a two-day presidential tour of the Yucatán Peninsula. At Puerto Progreso, she broke ground on the Multimodal Cargo Terminal — the freight extension of the Tren Maya rail network — with construction planned over 2.5 years, cargo service targeted for early 2027, and 26,200 direct jobs projected. She also inaugurated the Hospital General Naval at Yucalpetén and oversaw the next phase of Puerto Progreso's deep-water port expansion, accompanied by Yucatán Governor Joaquín Díaz Mena. Diplomatically, Mexico formally reaffirmed its support for former Chilean President Michelle Bachelet's candidacy to lead the United Nations as Secretary-General — coordinated with Brazil — in a meeting at the Palacio Nacional where Bachelet also met with Foreign Affairs Secretary Roberto Velasco.
